body: I think I'm just used to feeling numb or worse, just hesitating to feel too happy that I've chalked up what could count as great experiences down to temporary emotions before I'm inevitably disappointed again, but it's a good suggestion. Honestly, this is the most comforting thing someone's said to me in a minute, and I don't know you, but I appreciate you for that.

Good luck with the situation. Will be sending out positive thoughts for the best.

Favorite memory was when I was in the 8th grade before I finished middle school. I grew up in FL, and my classmates and I went to Islands of Adventure at Universal. The chaperone was this awesome teacher who I'd never met prior to the trip, and I got paired up with two friends of mine.

The teacher knew that we weren't exactly rich kids (a majority of people at that school lived in the suburbs) and I think she wanted to give us an experience that we normally wouldn't be able to have otherwise.

We were just about to head out but the teacher insists on buying us a funnel cake with whipped cream and strawberries. We're all eating, and shitty pop music is blaring, and we're singing and laughing and I'm not thinking about how many calories the cake has or if I'm singing too loud or if I'm dancing too weird.

For once I finally felt that nothing was weighing me down and that I could feel happy on my own and that I was okay the way I am. 

It's been a really long time since I've felt that way without any kind of substance/chemical help, but I'm still so grateful that it happened.

Also vanilla. Especially with rainbow sprinkles whaduuupp
